title: Choose an association test for independent categories
mathChecked: Independent review of the six requested after fields only. Pre-task count: prose 5, exhibit 18, combined 23 words (including visible labels and numbers); explanation 3 lines. Row totals = 50, 50; column totals = 50, 30, 20; N = 100. E_ij = row total x column total / N gives [25,15,10] in both rows; minimum E = 50 x 20 / 100 = 10 exactly. If columns are mutually exclusive patient categories, Pearson chi-square with (2-1)(3-1) = 2 degrees of freedom is appropriate. McNemar requires linked binary data; ANOVA requires a quantitative outcome. Arithmetic in the explanation is correct; no rounding.
fairness: 'Healed', 'Infected' and 'Bleeding' are not intrinsically mutually exclusive: an infected wound can also bleed, and healed status depends on assessment timing. The caption states independence but does not define one outcome category per patient. Pearson's ordinary contingency-table model needs each patient counted once in one column; overlapping event counts would invalidate that model.
suggestions: Define a single mutually exclusive wound-status classification at one assessment, with an explicit rule for infection plus bleeding, or replace these labels with naturally exclusive categories. Keep all six counts and the same single test-choice task. Do not treat the current caption alone as proof that overlapping clinical outcomes were coded correctly.
